Sleep and Mental Health

Source: vignettes/proposal.qmd

Introduction

For my final project, I would like to explore the relationship between sleep and mental health. I am interested in this topic because sleep is something that affects our daily lives, and I want to better understand whether people who get less sleep also tend to have worse mental health.

I plan to look at this relationship in two different populations: adults and high school students. I think it would be interesting to see whether similar patterns appear in both groups, even though they are at different stages of life.

Research Questions

  1. Is shorter sleep duration associated with more severe depressive symptoms among U.S. adults?

  2. Are high school students who report insufficient sleep more likely to report poor mental health?

  3. Do these associations differ across demographic groups, including sex and age or grade level?

Datasets

Datasets 1:NHANES 2017–2018

For my first analysis, I plan to use the 2017–2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), conducted by the CDC. I chose this dataset because it includes information about sleep duration and depressive symptoms. I plan to focus on adults aged 18 and older and explore variables such as sleep duration, PHQ-9 depression scores, age, and sex.

Dataset 2: Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS) 2023

For my second analysis, I would like to use the 2023 Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS), which collects information about health behaviors and experiences among U.S. high school students. I want to use this dataset to look at the relationship between sleep duration and self-reported mental health. I am also interested in whether the patterns differ by sex or grade level.

Proposed Analysis

I plan to use R for data cleaning, descriptive statistics, visualization, and exploratory statistical analysis.

First, I will summarize the distributions of sleep duration and mental health indicators in each dataset. Then, I will compare mental health outcomes across sleep-duration categories using tables and graphical displays.

Also, I will use regression models to examine associations between sleep duration and mental health outcomes while considering demographic factors. I will account for relevant survey design features when estimating population-level associations.

Expected Outcomes and Limitations

I expect to identify patterns in the relationship between sleep duration and mental health and to explore whether these patterns differ across population groups.

Because both datasets are observational and cross-sectional, this study will not establish causal relationships. Self-reported measures, missing data, differences in mental health measurement, and potential confounding may also affect interpretation.

The final project will present two separate analysis vignettes and document the data sources, methods, findings, uncertainties, and limitations.
